name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
hypothesis: Practical, long-tail tirzepatide questions people search (strength training, protein, side effects, stopping) beat approved-drug deep dives (median 8–17) and keep gaining views over time.
change: Lane A runs on every day without qualifying Lane C news (Lane P is paused). Practical tirzepatide topics only, long-tail searched question first, about 60 characters or fewer, at most 1 number. Cost, coverage and timeline-only topics are excluded. Slot, length and retention rules stay the same.
metric: Views and watch minutes at day 7 and day 28. Success: day-7 median views of 25 or more and watch-minute median of 60 or more, still growing at day 28.
min_sample: n=8 videos (expected about 11-03). Judge each video at day 7 and day 28.
result: Interim signal, on target so far. In-window in-lane videos (n=3): How Long 37 views/122 min, What to Eat 24/39, Side Effects 23/53 (day 3). Adding Strength Training (70/129, still climbing: 48 at day 9, 70 at day 11) gives n=4: median 30.5 views and about 88 min. These earned 91% of this week's new long-form watch minutes. Medicare (7 views, 0 min) is excluded as a cost topic.

name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed?', median about 105, n=7) would also work as long-form.
change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B, credited and dated, no sellers named.
metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median. Success: day-7 median of 33 or more.
result: Closed early at n=1. The pharmacy check got 8 views and 20 min. That's an anecdote, not proof the lane fails. We closed it because of the opportunity cost against Lane A and because the lane sits close to the 'online sources' policy line. Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public, named trial result with a headline number (ideally against tirzepatide or semaglutide) drives far more long-form views than evergreen topics (EloraTZP 575 views, 1,474 min).
change: Tightened: the long-form slot goes to the news only when all of these hold. The result first became public within 48 h. It's a named next-gen drug. It has a headline efficacy number from a randomized trial. Filings, Phase 1, food-effect and status-only news go to Shorts. Bare 'What Is [drug]?' explainers (Lane P) are paused.
metric: Day-7 views and watch minutes against the GLP-1 long-form median (24 views, 45 min). Success: day-7 median of 50 views or more.
min_sample: n=4 qualifying videos made after 10-20 (2–4 weeks, depending on news).
result: In-window n=1: petrelintide (10-25) had 4 views at day 2; score it on 11-01. Elecoglipron (10-26) isn't logged and was a decoder, so it counts as Lane P, not C. Looking back at fresh next-gen results with a headline number: EloraTZP 575, Orforglipron 59, Survodutide 47, retatrutide 29 and 18, CagriSema 24. That's a signal, carried by one outlier.

name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
hypothesis: A 20:00 funnel Short that asks a fresh question its live long-form answers, and carries a verified working link, will lift that long-form's daily views. Shorts get about 60 YouTube views each and currently send no measurable traffic to long-form.
change: Every 20:00 Short is a spin-off of a live long-form, rotating between that day's Lane C video, EloraTZP and Strength Training on Tirzepatide. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.' No spoken title. The publisher automatically puts a verified '▶ Full breakdown' link on description line 1. Topic rules don't change.
metric: The target long-form's viewCount in the 3 days after the Short against the 3 days before. Once traffic sources are exported, also 'Shorts feed' and 'related video' traffic. Success: average lift of 10 or more views a day, or 50% or more over baseline.
min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link. Shorts without a verified link are excluded.
result: Started 10-27; no data yet. Baseline: EloraTZP and Strength Training gained about 1–3 views a day before the experiment. Strength Training then jumped by about 11 a day (48 to 70 between day 9 and day 11), before the experiment, so use a per-video baseline.
